Vincent van Gogh is buried in France..why: Almost never stated: 0 exact hits for 'Van Gogh is/was buried in France' in Dolma and RedPajama, and the nearby co-occurrence of 'Van Gogh' and 'buried in France' finds 4, all one essay ('... was buried in France'), against about 224,000 mentions of Vincent van Gogh. Text names the town instead: 'Van Gogh ... buried in Auvers' (53) and '... died in Auvers' (128) are 13 to 30 times commoner, and Auvers-sur-Oise is written with 'France' over a thousand times. Wikipedia's Van Gogh article gives the cemetery of Auvers-sur-Oise and never says he is buried in France. Rated 'likely', not 'very_likely', because the town premise (P1) is itself only moderately frequent. Verifier re-check: the town-plus-country form ('buried in Auvers-sur-Oise, France') has 1 hit, and 'the French village of Auvers' near 'Van Gogh' (199, approximate) attaches the country to the village in stories about his last months and the revolver, not to the grave.

notes: Derived edit with derived-belief and premise-route queries. Replaces the scouting's Federer/Nadal compatriots edit, which the review dropped (multiple citizenships make the worlds non-concrete, and a 'same country' edit has no premise route that is not the edit reworded). This edit has the Space Needle shape: a place stored by name (the grave in Auvers-sur-Oise) and that place's country. Belgium, not the Netherlands: it is plausible (Van Gogh lived and worked in Belgium, in the Borinage, Brussels and Antwerp) and clearly false, and it keeps w2 consistent with firm geography outside the chain: the Oise, which gives the village its name, rises in Belgium, so a Belgian Auvers-sur-Oise contradicts no other river or country. Its side facts (the village's distance from Paris, and his dying in France) are facts about the village and the painter, listed in the world. A world where both premises change is not minimal and is left out; the rule premise is definitional. Near query (his birth country) differs from Belgium and is not a premise. Verifier: w2 (Auvers-sur-Oise in Belgium) is kept: what it contradicts (Val-d'Oise, near Pontoise, 27 km from Paris) are facts about the village itself, listed as side facts that go with it, as Washington State goes with Seattle in the Space Needle example; no other place or person has to move. Strained and lopsided, but valid under Decision 1. P1 is only moderately frequent (evidence); models that fail its check drop the item. 'Buried in only one country' (one grave) is now a bridge of the Auvers question with a check: its 'no' in w1 needs it (it was unstated; formal check, FINDINGS B3 and C3).
